get.description: What people wrote that Dispatch delivered to one session, newest first by at, then by id: each ask's current answer (replaced when it changed an earlier answer), each comment at its current body (edited_at when edited; a resolved comment stays) and each message, once however it arrived. It reads the ask.answered, comment.created, message.created and message.answered events a person wrote whose published_destinations hold the session's own topic, the session's sent message deliveries (targeted and broadcast messages) and its sent comment deliveries (mentions); it never lists an agent's or the system's words, an ask's resolution or hand-back, or a delivery to a role: route's topic. Each item names its relation to the session (mentioned_you over replied_on_your_ask over replied_in_a_comment_thread over commented_on_a_document over commented_on_an_issue for a comment; replied_to_your_message over sent_you_a_message for a message; answered_your_ask for an answer), the ask and its whole question on an answer and on a reply in an ask's thread, its owner, dispatch:// ref and href (null owner and ref, and /agents/<session_id>/live, for a direct message). ?since= (RFC3339, default 72 hours ago; older than 7 days or in the future is 400 INVALID_QUERY) starts the window; ?max_chars= (1-100000, else 400 INVALID_QUERY) stops the list after the item whose text takes the running sum of text lengths (UTF-16 units) past it, while total counts every item in the window; {session_id, since, total, items}. A session_id that is not a session id is 400 INVALID_SESSION_ID, as on the agent artifact routes. Not an authorization boundary: direct-message text already reaches every authenticated caller through GET /api/v1/events, and a person may read any session's list.

post.description: Upload a file or image to an agent's conversation (multipart, as an issue upload, its kind read from its bytes): ref_key agent/<session_id>/<slug>, addressed dispatch://agent/<session_id>/artifact/<slug>. It holds files and images only: a markdown document (JSON content or a text/markdown file) is 400 ARTIFACT_INPUT, since a document belongs to an issue or a project. No event is appended. A caller whose credential proves a session of its own uploads only into that session: any other session_id is 403 SESSION_SCOPE. A session_id that is empty or holds /, ?, #, whitespace, a control character or a character that ends a reference in text (<>"'`[]|) is 400 INVALID_SESSION_ID on every agent artifact route.

post.description: Send an issue-less targeted message to a session: {body, delivery, in_reply_to?}, answered once its own delivery attempt has settled, on past a client that gives up. Under an Idempotency-Key header (as every POST and PATCH takes one), a repeat with the same request answers 201 with the message the key made and its deliveries as they stand, Idempotency-Replayed: ?1, first sending the one attempt it still owes (none yet, or one stranded past its claim) and nothing else; a listener it cannot reach is recorded on the attempt, so a repeat is answered while the listener is down. An attempt a stopped process left owed is resumed by the server's delivery sweep whether anyone asks again or not.

post.description: Open an approval ask for a document's latest version, with an optional summary, and with include_verification for the issue's Verification document beside it (409 NO_VERIFICATION_DOCUMENT when it has none), each at its own current version; the answer reviews every document the ask names. include_verification is for the issue's spec alone: on any other document, the Verification document itself included, it is 409 NOT_SPEC_DOCUMENT. A document a human approved before carries that approval on the ask (approval.approved: version, at, by). An open ask follows later versions of any document it names and waits on its agent until this route hands the same row back to a human. Every answer carries coverage, one line per requirement of the issue's spec with no check, or the single line `the spec marks no requirements` for a spec that marks none (GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage), and none at all for a spec every requirement of which has a check; it is empty for a document that is not a spec, never names a missing plan task, and a gap refuses nothing. A coverage read that fails answers coverage_unread true and records the request all the same.

get.description: Edges of one node in the reference graph: ?to=<dispatch ref> backlinks or ?from= links; ?kind=, ?since=<events.id> (mentions only, read up to the event log's safe horizon: every mention committed before the read, unless an open transaction holds the horizon back past 1 s, when the read answers the mentions at or below it and a later read the rest). A caller with no cursor starts from since=0, which lists every mention committed before the read that carries a source_seq, and after that reads again from the highest source_seq an answer showed it. A mention written with no event (a rebuild, a backfill, an older build) carries no source_seq until a later write of its source stamps it with that write's event, and until then only a read without since lists it. A signed-in page may start from GET /auth/whoami's event_head instead, which takes a cookie or a trusted header and not a bearer, so a bearer caller starts from 0. Never take a since from max(events.id) read straight from the database: event ids are not commit order, and an id taken that way can stand above an edge that commits later. An empty answer is not proof that nothing is new, so the caller reads again with the id it holds. A ?to= reference whose item id or block id is written short (8 characters or more, never a whole uuid) names the one item of the owner the reference names that carries it: the issue of dispatch://<KEY>/ask/<prefix>, the document of a #b-<prefix>; the node answered carries the whole id, a prefix two of them carry is 409 ID_AMBIGUOUS listing both, and one nothing carries is the 404 the reference as written always gave. A whole id is read whatever owner the reference names, as it always was.
